text.p: Britain's second biggest clothing retailer Burton Group Plc said on Thursday profits were up 22.7 percent in the first half and the second half sales were up 11 percent overall.

The retailer, owner of Debenhams, Top Shop and Dorothy Perkins, reported first half profits of 108.1 million pounds, up from 88.1 million a year ago. Sales, excluding mail order, rose to 1.17 billion pounds from 1.09 billion.
Burton, which has achieved a major turnaround from troubles in the early 1990s, said sales, excluding home shopping, were up 6.8 percent in the first 10 weeks of the second half.
Gross margins rose by 0.7 percentage points overall, and by 0.6 points excluding home shopping.
Chairman Sir John Hoskyns said the group had done well. "The group has had a good half. Debenhams is performing strongly. The multiples (womenswear stores) continue to make good progress."

Burton said it plans to redevelop and extend its flagship Top Shop store at Oxford Circus in London. American sportswear brand Nike will take 73,000 square feet in the store for what will be the first NikeTown shop outside the United States.
Debenhams, the department store, will open nine more outlets over the next four years, creating 3,400 jobs throughout Britain.
